artifacts.notes: Extent as the retrieving lane measured it: Complete case, State ex rel. Garrett v. McPeters, 256 Ala. 555-559: the per curiam judgment, Brown J.'s dissent in full, and the opinion on rehearing, with star page markers through the passage at *556. READ THE DISSENT AND THE JUDGMENT APART. The per curiam majority ousted the sheriff; Brown J., dissenting, casts the convicted sheriff as the victim. An entry presenting that figure as the court's own holding misdescribes the case, and the retrieving lane says so expressly.
artifacts.rights_basis: A judicial opinion of a court of the United States and its official reporter carry no copyright: under the government edicts doctrine the works of judges in their judicial capacity are not copyrightable, and the retrieving research lane of run efff3a6f73c1f451 recorded the same finding for every member of this set, in the form 'US court opinions and official reporters; public domain'. The file is the reporter's text with the Caselaw Access Project's minimal star-pagination markup and nothing else -- no navigation, no styling, no site apparatus. The bytes are retained at 0.02 MB so that a reader with no network can reopen the sentence a claim quotes; guidance/sources.md makes that the default and names size as the only other exemption, which a file this small cannot reach. BOUND, stated rather than assumed: the Caselaw Access Project's own terms for its transcriptions were not read by the retrieving lane and were not read here, so the basis above is the opinion's own status in law and not a grant by that project.
